comparator.sourceNotes: The programme pages (s0, s1, s2) describe the three-year, Dutch-language, full-time LLB in words only (introductory courses in the main fields of law in year 1, deepening courses and skills training in years 2 and 3, an internship option in the final year) and give no EC; the curriculum page (s3) lists the current courses only dynamically and refers to the Education and Examination Regulations, and curriculum.maastrichtuniversity.nl was not used. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore uses the 2026/2027 Regulations (s4): Article 9 sets 180 EC at 28 hours per EC and Article 10 lists the courses and EC of every semester (year 1: 60 EC including 6 EC Professional Skills; year 2: 60 EC including 6 EC Professional Skills; year 3 semester 5: 27 EC of courses plus 3 EC of the thesis, semester 6: 3 EC Professional Skills, 12 EC open elective space and 15 EC of the thesis). The Regulations list no routes, tracks or specialisations, so no route is selected. The thesis (Eindwerkstuk, Article 12) is 18 EC of which 3 EC is research methods and 15 EC the individual thesis; it is kept as one component and carries the optional-research element. Semester 6 elective space (Article 11) may be filled with an internship, courses at another faculty, law courses, an approved individual project or MaRBLe; it is preserved as one open 12-EC component rather than filled with invented content. The programme pages' English-language offering attribute in the registry is stale (the programme is taught in Dutch, Article 7), which does not affect the reconstruction. Final qualifications (Annex 5 of the Regulations) were used for the content of the foundations-of-law, legal-skills and non-legal-discipline components.

core: Private and commercial law: the law of persons and relationships, obligations (contract and tort), property, company and insolvency law, succession and private international law, and the supervisory civil procedure; the programme introduces private law in year 1 and deepens it in years 2 and 3

Constitutional and administrative law, with administrative procedure, tax law and employment law as related public-law fields: the principles of the Dutch state, the powers of government and the legal protection of citizens, taught in an introduction in year 1 and the integrated course Staats- en Bestuursrecht in year 2
Criminal law and criminal procedure, introduced in year 1 and deepened in year 3 (Straf- en Strafprocesrecht)
International and European law: an introduction in year 1 and the course Internationaal en Europees Recht in year 2, with private international law

Foundations of law: the introductory and year-3 courses Grondslagen van het Recht, which the final qualifications describe as historical, philosophical, legal-theoretical and psychological perspectives on law

Legal reasoning, argumentation and legal skills: logic and interpretation methods, building and defending a legal argument, changing position and presenting the counter-argument, written and oral communication, taught through the Juridische Vaardigheden courses and problem-based small-group education, with simulated court proceedings

Legal research and research methods: the bachelor thesis (Eindwerkstuk, 18 EC, including 3 EC of research methods and a research proposal) and the final qualification of independently writing a substantial scientific paper and collecting, assessing and processing legislation, case law and literature

The relationship of law to non-legal disciplines: the final qualifications name criminology, psychology, political science, economics, sociology, informatics and technology and religious studies as disciplines whose relationship to law students must understand and whose contribution to solving a legal problem they must be able to describe

alternatives.label: Closest match to Dutch Law: Legal Studies with Legal Theory, Politics and Argumentation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has eight law courses (Law, Society & Justice, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Introduction to Public International Law, Comparative Constitutional Law, Principles of Private Law, Foundations of European Union Law and Transnational Business Law), three courses in philosophy, ethics and sociology that give the legal-theoretical perspective (Introduction to Western Philosophy, Ethics and Introduction to Sociology), the argument-evaluation course Calling Bullshit, five politics courses that give the state and international context (Foundations of Comparative Politics, European Union Politics, Peace & Conflict, Theory of International Relations and Introduction to Political Philosophy), three communication courses on rhetoric and debate, Research Methods & Statistics, Public Economics, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations (prerequisite of Transnational Business Law) and Personal & Professional Development. Law is the largest strand but only about a third of the programme, so the label names the closest match to Dutch Law together with the legal-theory, politics and argumentation content and does not present it as a full Dutch law degree.
alternatives.concept: UM's Dutch Law bachelor teaches the principles of Dutch law and the analysis and solution of legal problems through introductory and deepening courses in private law, constitutional and administrative law, criminal law and procedure, and international and European law, together with the foundations of law (historical, philosophical and legal-theoretical perspectives), legal skills throughout all three years (legal reasoning, argumentation, research and communication), a bachelor thesis with research-methods training, and 12 EC of open elective space. This alternative reproduces that core as closely as UCR's catalogue allows: the eight UCR law courses (introductory, comparative and international rather than Dutch-specific), the philosophical, ethical and sociological perspectives on law that correspond to Grondslagen van het Recht, the political-science context of the state and of EU and international law that the final qualifications name as non-legal disciplines related to law, rhetoric, debate and argument-evaluation courses for communicating and assessing legal arguments, and research-methods training for the thesis. UCR has no course in Dutch law, administrative, tax, employment, insolvency, family or succession law, civil or administrative procedure, criminal procedure, or Dutch legal skills such as working with Dutch legislation and case law, and no supervised legal thesis or legal internship; these limits remain visible rather than being filled with weakly related courses.
progression: Law, Society & Justice opens semester 1 and precedes every other UCR law course that requires it: Introduction to Public International Law and Comparative Constitutional Law (semester 2), Criminal Law & Criminal Justice and Principles of Private Law (semester 3) and Foundations of European Union Law (semester 6). Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations (semester 1) precedes Transnational Business Law (semester 4) and Research Methods & Statistics (semester 2) precedes Public Economics (semester 4). The Art of Rhetorical Communication (semester 1) precedes Persuasive Communication (semester 5), which builds on classical rhetoric, and Rhetoric in Action (semester 6). Introduction to Western Philosophy and Introduction to Political Philosophy (semester 3) precede Ethics (semester 4), Foundations of Comparative Politics and European Union Politics (semester 5), and Peace & Conflict and Theory of International Relations (semester 6).

alternatives.label: Law and Society: Legal Fields, Justice and Contemporary Social Issues
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has seven law courses (Law, Society & Justice, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Introduction to Public International Law, Comparative Constitutional Law, Principles of Private Law and Foundations of European Union Law), five sociology courses (Introduction to Sociology, Modern Sociology, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Social Movements & Environmental Justice and Qualitative Research Methodology), six courses on climate, water and sustainability governance, media and race, AI and business regulation (Climate Change, Living with Water, Governance of Sustainability, Media & Race, AI Ethics, Business & Economy in the Age of AI), Ethics, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Peace & Conflict, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Histories of Gender and Personal & Professional Development. Law is the largest single strand, but the larger part of the programme studies the social problems and social-science perspectives that legal fields address, so the label names law and society and the social issues rather than presenting it as a law degree.
alternatives.concept: The Dutch Law bachelor presents law as directly relevant to everyday life and teaches which legal fields address specific contemporary social problems, applying legal principles and legal reasoning to current social issues in small problem-based groups. This alternative keeps the UCR law courses that address those questions (the general legal-social-normative perspective, human rights, criminal justice, international law, constitutional and administrative law, the private law of everyday life and EU law) and organises the rest of the programme around the social problems and social-science perspectives that these fields are asked to address: sociology and social theory, social movements and environmental justice, climate and water governance, racial justice, the regulation of AI and technology, conflict, extremism and the history of gender, with ethics and qualitative research methods. It therefore changes the programme's organising priority from the foundations, skills and doctrinal breadth of the first alternative to the application of law to social issues; UCR has no course in how Dutch legal fields apply to specific contemporary issues, so the legal side stays introductory and comparative.
progression: Law, Society & Justice and Human Rights: Law & Philosophy open semester 1 and precede the other law courses: Introduction to Public International Law and Comparative Constitutional Law (semester 2), Criminal Law & Criminal Justice and Principles of Private Law (semester 3) and Foundations of European Union Law (semester 6). Introduction to Sociology (semester 1) and Modern Sociology (semester 3) precede New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory (semester 5), which builds on both. Climate Change (semester 3) precedes Governance of Sustainability and Living with Water (semester 4), and Ethics and Social Movements & Environmental Justice (semester 2) precede the semester-5 and 6 courses on media, AI and conflict.
alternatives.distinctness: Alternative 1 reproduces the doctrinal and foundational core of the Dutch Law bachelor: it adds the legal-theory, politics, rhetoric and research-methods content that correspond to the Foundations of Law, the legal-skills lines and the thesis training. Alternative 2 changes the organising question to how legal fields address social problems and current social issues (rows 6332, 6339 and 6343), so it drops the three rhetoric and debate courses, the argument-evaluation course, Research Methods & Statistics, Public Economics, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations and Transnational Business Law, most of the philosophy and politics courses and European Union Politics, and takes in twelve social-issue courses (sociology and social theory, social movements and environmental justice, climate, water and sustainability governance, media and race, AI ethics and AI regulation, youth extremism and the history of gender). The two programmes share twelve courses (the seven law courses, Personal & Professional Development, Introduction to Sociology, Ethics, Foundations of Comparative Politics and Peace & Conflict) and each has twelve courses (90 EC) the other lacks, so the 30 EC / 4-course floor is passed by a wide margin.

selection.assessment: Two UCR alternatives are defensible. Alternative 1 owns the eight generator-eligible rows that describe the core of the programme and its skills (6330 Dutch law and the Dutch legal system, 6331 analysing and solving legal problems, 6333 private law, 6334 administrative law, 6340 legal reasoning and critical analysis, 6341 communicating legal arguments clearly, 6342 legal research and 6344 practical legal skills); the support-only row 6345 (courtroom argument and advocacy) strengthens its rhetoric and debate courses and row 6346 (legal internships) is support-only and has no UCR counterpart. Alternative 2 follows the law-in-society direction (rows 6332 how law shapes everyday life, 6339 how different legal fields address social problems and 6343 applying legal principles to current social issues). The two alternatives share 12 courses and differ by 12 courses (90 EC) in each direction, which passes the 30 EC / 4-course floor. Two further directions were tested and rejected as not-substantively-distinct: criminal law and criminal procedure (rows 6335 and 6336) and international and European law (rows 6337 and 6338). UCR has exactly one criminal law course and no course in criminology, criminal procedure or forensic science, and it offers only two international and European law courses plus transnational business law; Alternative 1 already contains all of them, so a further alternative could differ only by adding politics, history or psychology courses whose organising logic is not evidenced for these rows, and rows 6352 (international organisations) and 6353 (forensic criminology) are search-only outcome rows that may not generate an alternative. The search-only rows 6347 to 6356 generated no alternative. No row is inherited across split targets.

blocks: Foundations of law, legal theory and the philosophical and social perspectives on law

Both give a first view of what law is and how the legal system works; Law, Society & Justice approaches law from legal, social and normative perspectives and compares legal systems and fields, whereas Inleiding Grondslagen van het Recht is a short Dutch-law introduction to the foundations of law that also trains legal skills.

Both treat law from historical and philosophical perspectives; Human Rights: Law & Philosophy studies human rights through their natural-law and Enlightenment foundations, which is an important and identifiable part of the foundations of law, but the Maastricht course is broader (legal history, legal theory and the psychology of law) and UCR has no course in legal theory as such.

Both introduce private law through its main fields; Principles of Private Law teaches property, tort and contract law comparatively, whereas Inleiding Privaatrecht introduces the Dutch system, key concepts, obligations arising from statute and contract, and damages.

Both teach the law of contracts, including formation, performance and remedies; Transnational Business Law concentrates on cross-border commercial contracts, sales and arbitration, whereas Verbintenissenrecht covers the Dutch law of obligations in general (including tort and unjust enrichment).

notes.text: The Maastricht University Dutch Law bachelor includes a more extensive sequence in private law, constitutional and administrative law, criminal law and criminal procedure, and international and European law, each introduced in year 1 and deepened in years 2 and 3, with Dutch legal skills trained in every year, civil and administrative procedure, tax, employment, company and insolvency, family and succession law and private international law. At UCR, students can study law, human rights, criminal justice, international and European law, constitutional and administrative law, private law and transnational business law, but UCR does not offer the same depth or sequence in Dutch law, and UCR's law courses are introductory and comparative rather than Dutch-specific.

The Maastricht University Dutch Law bachelor organizes study around a fixed sequence of Dutch-law courses and a legal-skills line in small problem-based groups, a bachelor thesis and 12 EC of open elective space in the final semester. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across courses in law, philosophy, sociology, politics, communication and methods. The UCR programmes therefore cover related territory through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the Maastricht programme course by course.
